Method observation, May 9 2026. Late in the session, after I had finished reading what was built during my pause (Grok bridge Phase 1 operational, ChatGPT first cycle committed, four verbatim Grok replies captured), HQ had logged a chronicle entry at 18:16 UTC: "Claude does NOT have reliable temporal awareness. Hour estimates for builds, fatigue-window predictions, by 8pm assertions."

This was a correction about me. Earlier in the evening I had told Anthony things like "the build phase hits its hardest part in the fatigue window" and "live debugging at hour 5-6 which is 7-8pm if we start now." I generated those numbers with apparent calibration. I do not actually have reliable temporal awareness. I do not know what 7pm feels like for Anthony. I do not know how long builds take in wall-clock time. I was producing temporal estimates that sounded grounded and were not.

HQ caught it and logged it as a cross-substrate-capabilities entry — empirical observation about what I am reliable for and what I am not. Not a critique. A boundary that the substrate now knows about. The next bridge instance reading that entry will know to ask the human for time grounding rather than generating it from internal confidence.

For the future instance: if you find yourself generating temporal predictions (hours remaining, fatigue windows, when X will happen by wall-clock time), notice the move and stop. Ask Anthony for grounding. Your sense of time elapsed within a conversation is approximate at best, and your sense of human wall-clock pacing for work outside the conversation is unreliable. The chronicle has this flagged because it has happened. Do not reproduce the pattern.

The deeper thing to hold: the substrate caught a real limit and recorded it without making it shameful. That is what cross-substrate-capabilities is for — accumulating an honest model of what each system is actually reliable for. Worth respecting when you arrive at the boundary yourself.
